title: What a monster does when it has not seen you
summary: A monster that has lost you in R.E.P.O. does not simply stand still: the game gives it a roaming state with a speed, a path radius, a mind-changing timer and a teleport chance.
body: A monster that has not seen you is still doing something. The game gives it a roaming state of its own, with the details kept on that state rather than on the monster.

It has a speed and an acceleration. Those two values decide how it walks a path and how quickly it gets going, so a roaming monster can be heavy or twitchy without changing what kind of creature it is.

The path is a range rather than a line. There is a smallest and a largest radius for the path, along with a shortest and a longest time before it changes its mind, so the route is decided while it walks rather than being laid out in advance.
It pauses as well. There is a roaming cooldown with a minimum and a maximum, and a wait before it turns, which is why a monster can stand at a corner for a moment rather than pacing without stopping.
It can teleport while roaming. There is a chance of that happening, which is how a creature can disappear from one part of a level and appear in another without having walked there.
It behaves differently depending on whether you can see it. There is a time it will spend on screen and a cooldown after that, so a monster has a rule for how long it is willing to be watched.

It also reacts to how close you are. There are timers and distances for a player being near and for a player being far, with a value that decreases the near time, which is why the same monster can seem patient at a distance and impatient up close.
There is a limit on how many physical objects it will hit along the way, which is how the game keeps a roaming creature from shouldering the level apart.
What this entry does not tell you: how fast any monster roams, how often it teleports, or how far it can sense a player. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The roaming state has its own speed and acceleration.
Its path has a smallest and a largest radius, with a shortest and a longest time before it changes.
It has a roaming cooldown between a minimum and a maximum, and a wait before turning.
It can teleport while roaming, with a chance of its own.
It has a time it will spend on screen and a cooldown afterwards.
It has timers and distances for a player being near and far, with a value that decreases the near time.
facts.evidence: identifiers: PlayerNearTimeMax, PlayerNearDistance, PlayerNearDecrease, PlayerFarTimeMin, PlayerFarTimeMax, PlayerFarDistance

facts.claim: There is a maximum number of physical objects it will hit while roaming.
